deep.reconstruction:
This folio is effectively blank. Its only visible text is faint mirror-image show-through of the following leaf, 287.a, headed 'Ableitung der Gleichungen pag. 287' (derivation of the equations of p. 287). The reconstruction below is therefore of that show-through derivation. Its task is to solve cos(f − i g) = p + i q for real f and g, i.e. to invert the cosine of a complex argument (equivalently, to express arccos(p+iq) in real terms).

Setup:
- c = cos f, s = sin f.
- γ = cos(ig) = cosh g, and sin(ig) = iσ with σ = sinh g.
- Expanding cos f cos(ig) + sin f sin(ig) = cγ + i(sσ) gives four relations:
  (1) c² + s² = 1
  (2) γ² − σ² = 1
  (3) cγ = p
  (4) sσ = q

Eliminating s and σ:
- Squaring (4) and using (1), (2): (1 − c²)(γ² − 1) = q².
- Expanding and using (3): γ² + c² − 1 − c²γ² = q², hence γ² + c² = 1 + p² + q².
- Adding and subtracting 2cγ = 2p (step made explicit by me): (γ + c)² = (1+p)² + q² and (γ − c)² = (1−p)² + q².
- So γ + c = √((1+p)² + q²) and γ − c = √((1−p)² + q²).

The sums for s and σ:
- s² + σ² = γ² − c² = (γ+c)(γ−c) = √(((1+p)² + q²)((1−p)² + q²)).
- s² − σ² = 2 − c² − γ² = 1 − p² − q² (no square root).

Polar forms:
- 1 + p = a cos A, q = a sin A, so a = |1 + z| with z = p + iq.
- 1 − p = b cos B, q = b sin B, so b = |1 − z|.
- Then s² + σ² = ab.
- Also ab cos(A+B) = (1+p)(1−p) − q² = 1 − p² − q², so s² − σ² = ab cos(A+B).
- Half-angle formulas give s² = ab cos²((A+B)/2) and σ² = ab sin²((A+B)/2).
- Hence s = √(ab)·cos((A+B)/2) and σ = √(ab)·sin((A+B)/2).
- The signs are consistent with (4), because sσ = (ab/2) sin(A+B) = (q(1−p) + q(1+p))/2 = q.

Final result:
- γ = cosh g = (a+b)/2 = (|1+z| + |1−z|)/2.
- c = cos f = (a−b)/2 = (|1+z| − |1−z|)/2.

This is the classical real-variable formula for arccos of a complex number. Geometrically, the point (p, q) lies on the confocal ellipse with foci ±1 given by g = const and on the confocal hyperbola given by f = const (elliptic coordinates). Context on the previous page is unrelated: determinant identities and the binomial mean error √(αβn).

Transcription (both this page and the next) gives s² − σ² = √(1 − p² − q²). Mathematically it equals 1 − p² − q² with no square root. Either Gauss slipped or the root sign belongs to the transcription; it does not affect the following lines, which correctly use ab cos(A+B).
The next-page transcription gives s² + σ² = √(ab); correct is ab, as the show-through on this page reads.
The step from γ² + c² = 1 + p² + q² to γ ± c = √((1±p)² + q²) silently uses 2cγ = 2p. This is correct.
Choosing positive roots for γ ± c presumes g ≥ 0 and the branch with γ + c ≥ 0 and γ − c ≥ 0. This is fine, since cosh g ≥ |cos f|.

results.what: Solution of cos(f − i g) = p + i q: cosh g = (|1+z| + |1−z|)/2, cos f = (|1+z| − |1−z|)/2, with sin f and sinh g given by √(ab)·cos and √(ab)·sin of (A+B)/2, where A = arg(1+z) and B = arg(1−z).
results.modern_name: Real/imaginary parts of the complex arccosine (arccos z via |z+1| and |z−1|); elliptic coordinates with foci ±1
results.usually_credited_to: Classical complex trigonometry (Euler, later 18th–19th c.); the |z±1| form is standard in handbooks (e.g. Abramowitz–Stegun 4.4.37)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine inversion of the cosine of a complex argument, of a kind Gauss used in conformal mapping and geodesy. Nothing beyond standard early-19th-century complex trigonometry. The folio itself is blank apart from show-through.
